chapter_keywords: a record of a mortal's journey to immortality
chapter_seo_title: A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality Ch. 576: The Celestial Omen
chapter_meta_description: Yuan Yao begins the Soul Reunion Art, but the massive celestial omen it creates attracts unwanted attention from nearby sects. Han Li’s guard duty just got a lot more complicated.
og_description: A forbidden ritual starts, and the sky itself screams a warning to every cultivator for miles.
twitter_description: Han Li helps Yuan Yao set up defenses for a risky ritual, which immediately creates a sky-wide celestial alarm.

lore_anchors.definition: A dark, Yin-aligned technique used to reunite a shattered or fading primordial soul with a prepared vessel, often at great cost to the caster.
The condensed spiritual essence of a high-level cultivator, capable of independent existence and possession; preserving it requires a suitable physical anchor.
A special coffin made from Cold Jade, used to preserve a corpse or a fading soul within a Yin-rich environment.
The first major stage of cultivation, where a practitioner absorbs and refines spiritual Qi within their body.
The second major stage of cultivation, marking the creation of a stable internal foundation for higher arts.
The third major stage, where a cultivator condenses their power into a Golden Core, dramatically increasing lifespan and combat ability.
A visible disturbance in the sky caused by a world-shaking event, such as a forbidden art or powerful treasure emerging, which attracts the attention of cultivators nearby.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Yuan Yao have to shatter her core?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Soul Reunion Art requires an immense, precise expenditure of Yin-type energy to call back and stabilize a fading primordial soul. Yuan Yao’s Golden Core is the most powerful, concentrated source of energy she has—sacrificing it provides the necessary power for the ritual to succeed.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn't Han Li just stop her?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the Mortal Stream, a deeply personal debt is a powerful motivator that can override cold logic. Han Li recognizes that her decision is a calculated sacrifice based on a lifetime of loyalty, so after a single clarifying question, he accepts her choice and focuses on his role as protector.
